title: Code Mode with agent teams, startup checks, hundreds of fixes
headline: Code Mode can run alongside agent teams, startup flags and settings get clearer warnings, and a very large batch of fixes covers sign-in, MCP, Remote Control, agents and the terminal display.

lines.text: Code Mode can now be turned on with agent teams enabled; if it was already on, sessions with teams now start in Code Mode.
Claude Code warns at startup when an --allowedTools, --disallowedTools or --tools entry doesn't look like a complete rule.
When an administrator adds managed-mcp.json during a session, a message explains why MCP servers stop loading.
/status gets a row saying when your provider or a variable like DISABLE_TELEMETRY turns features off.
/plugin and claude plugin list note when a malformed plugin.json field such as author or homepage is ignored.
New hints: Ctrl+O reveals hidden startup notices, the empty prompt says what to do after a failed request, and a subagent's view shows "esc to stop" where Esc stops it.
OTEL_RESOURCE_INCLUDE_HOST adds host.name and host.id to OpenTelemetry resource attributes; it's off by default.
Mods gain overflowX="scroll" on Box, and maxLines and wrap="clip" on Text.
cp is no longer refused when only the source file falls under an Edit deny rule.
Bash commands that delete or overwrite files are no longer summarized as searches or reads, and the "Dangerous rm operation" warning no longer appears on hard-to-parse commands without rm.
Background sessions stop before any model request when they lose your shell's LLM gateway, and the background service no longer kills your own processes when a process number was reused.
Rules added in /permissions or at a tool prompt, and /add-dir folders, no longer look saved when the settings file couldn't be written; the terminal warns and names it.
A failing MCP headersHelper, or one skipped in an untrusted folder, no longer makes other sessions start without that server.

Settings fixes: certain managed key names no longer block startup, values nested past 64 levels are dropped with a warning instead of crashing, and a file saved with an error mid-session now triggers a warning.
The subagent model from managed settings now applies in Claude Desktop's Code tab, overriding yours as in the terminal, unless those settings also choose a provider or gateway.
On Linux, sandboxed commands start when home or config is a symlink into /net with reads denied, and stopping mid-command no longer leaves empty placeholder files like .git/config.lock.
Stray keys no longer answer Yes at a nested folder trust prompt or accept the auto mode default offer, and a message typed over that offer is kept.
A note typed on a permission prompt is no longer sent after Tab hid it.
Managed PreToolUse hooks that refuse a direct tool call now leave an OpenTelemetry tool_decision event and a permission_denials entry.
Letters typed over /sandbox or a delete question in /permissions no longer move the selection.
Resumed sessions keep recent turns after a crash following an empty reply and keep history when memory ran low, and a background session isn't killed when you touch the older session it resumed.
On Linux Remote Control and cloud sessions, a re-sent file no longer overwrites Claude's changed copy; the copy moves to a .kept- folder or the new file isn't saved.
claude purge shows its prompts on the terminal even with stdout redirected, and the spend limit menu no longer drops the monthly limit on quick Backspace and Enter.

/rewind fixes: all files restore after running /branch twice during a slow backup, untracked shell changes read "Code changes unknown", Esc cancels its summary, and its list and warnings show properly.
Ctrl+C or Ctrl+D twice in /skills saves and closes the panel, the usage limit menu no longer erases your draft, and recalled drafts keep pasted text and images.

Input fixes: edited answers send the new text, revisiting an answered question keeps your answer, /feedback and /bug don't send on a space or lose text, and a prompt after a list option isn't dropped.
/plan <description> uses the description even when plan mode is already on.
Valid PDFs stay in the conversation when the API rejects another PDF read alongside them, and one failed memory allocation while drawing no longer ends the session.
Compaction on Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry or with telemetry off summarizes properly, and image-heavy Vertex AI sessions compact and retry instead of sticking on a 30 MB limit error.
A max_tokens value above the model's limit now triggers a retry at the maximum the API reports.
grep in the Bash tool no longer silently skips some text files.
A crashed Node or Python hook now shows its error, and Ctrl+O shows up to 10,000 characters of output.
/goal clear or a new /goal typed while Stop hooks and background work run now sticks.
The automatic session recap is no longer sent after a reply billed to usage credits; /recap still works.
Auto mode no longer stays on its local classifier, which counts toward usage, because of a stale saved value.
Sign-in fixes: the Console option no longer replaces a subscription login made with your Claude plan, and /login, "Not logged in" and /status say when an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is or isn't in use.

More sign-in fixes: logout clears Console profile credentials on unusual drives, resumed agent-view chats use the right credentials, a one-off 401 in Desktop's Code tab is retried, and network block pages aren't mistaken for expired logins.
Sign-in screens show a pasted code, display "Finishing sign-in…" after submitting, and Esc goes back while waiting for the browser.
Logging out or quitting at sign-in and first-run steps leaves a clean screen, and Ctrl+C twice works on the theme choice without freezing setup screens.
/privacy-settings and the terms prompt save exactly what you chose, on the right account, and report failed saves.
In Code Mode, skills and commands with an inline ! command needing approval now load in auto mode (Claude is asked to run it), including when a background subagent preloads them.
Mods can use Bash, Read and other tools through $.tool.call and $.tool.check in Code Mode.
MCP fixes: parallel calls no longer read each other's results, tool search loads the right server's tool by exact name, and prompts from servers with near-identical names stay visible.

More MCP fixes: no reconnecting to a server an SDK host removed, Claude learns of declined server questions and unavailable resource tools, and anyOf or oneOf schemas accept values like 42 as numbers.
/mcp shows why a local stdio server failed, Esc closes a reconnect wait while it continues in the background, and Enable shows progress without a second Enter undoing it.
claude mcp add-json explains what to fix, and MCP screens get correct Ctrl+C hints, clean URL copying, and Tab between form fields.
Remote Control stays connected through brief server outages, shows its full QR code in small windows, reports busy and waiting states correctly, and Stop from a phone ends background subagents too.
A reply stopped during a restart no longer runs again in remote sessions, and Stop in cloud and self-hosted sessions no longer waits for slow MCP servers.
Files sent from cloud and Remote Control sessions get a second try after proxy errors, and claude.ai chats and Cowork tasks send approved files and scan zip-type Office files for secrets.
Self-hosted runners stop requesting tokens nonstop with a fast clock, /autofix-pr links a session it couldn't stop, and /teleport no longer hides sessions in narrow terminals.

Artifact fixes: files in a background session's temp folder can be published, subagents denied Artifact don't get its tools, folder access is described correctly, and the terminal shows the link after publishing.

The main conversation learns which agent a messaged subagent reports to, background agents aren't told you refused a call when the session ended, and queued messages stay out of a viewed subagent's prompt.
Agent rows under the prompt now show waiting, stopped, failed and retrying states correctly, /tasks names each background command's subagent, and the launch line counts every agent started.

Agent display fixes: old "done" lines don't show running shells, auto mode tool counts skip the final report, the header shows a viewed teammate's model, pasted images reach background agents, and long results align.
claude --worktree shows progress during a slow setup, and the exit dialog no longer counts a new folder as one file.
After a failed call, workflow resume tells Claude how many results were reused and where reuse stopped.
Malformed glob patterns no longer hang settings, marketplace entries or Grep filters, and plugin requests through an unresponsive ALL_PROXY fail after 25 seconds.
The / menu, /skills and /plugin handle duplicate names, search boxes accept IME input, dictation and fast typing, the /plugin cursor returns after clearing, and a mod's truncated Text keeps its rows.
/model's Default row names your plan's default model, and choosing it in the terminal switches you back to it.
A skill, command or agent created during a session is found right away, and /clear --help shows usage instead of clearing; /help <command> is added.
Retries after server errors show a spinner and "retrying…" instead of a frozen reply or "Retrying in 0s", and the countdown keeps moving.
Streaming no longer drops transcript rows, makes the prompt or text jump, or hides replies behind a long queued message.
Fullscreen fixes: no text jumps when replies finish or windows resize, no blank transcript on long searches or fast scrolls, and the pinned prompt shows the right question.
The screen no longer blanks after picking a model or scrambles after /tui default, and long new files or very long shell commands no longer freeze it.
Prompt editing fixes: Shift+Enter right after a paste adds a line, the cursor lands on the right row of wrapped prompts, and undo keeps your last words.
Pasted code and diffs keep indentation and colors in the transcript, image placeholders land correctly and resend after Ctrl+Y, and asterisks in your prompts stay visible.
claude -p now prints to the terminal while retrying a failing API request or when it fails with output redirected.
Windows paths in replies keep backslashes before folders like .claude, and bold text in Japanese, Chinese and Korean renders when it starts or ends with punctuation.
/memory warns when the file it opens is read-only.
Claude no longer edits keybindings.json for Claude Desktop shortcuts, where it has no effect, or claims an admin can enable Claude in Chrome when policy disables it.
Suggested prompts are no longer bare tags, and cut-off command output names the file holding the full text.
Collapsed tool lines show the real state of calls awaiting permission, failed, blocked or stopped, and failed turns and skill or agent calls no longer show "done" or "Initializing…".
/btw says when the model tried to use a tool, and long /btw answers can be scrolled and show they're still coming.
/resume search finds older sessions and treats typed numbers as search text, and Ctrl+R again in fullscreen prompt search moves to the next older match.
Tab in shell mode completes names without a slash and quotes paths with spaces, and a rebound chat:submit key works with menus open.
Esc over typed text no longer opens Rewind or cancels a pending /loop, and "Esc again to clear" disappears when it no longer applies.
Typing in a question's note lands in the right place, and paste hints no longer hide the mode, "esc to interrupt" or the middle of very long pastes.
claude --help piped into a pager like less now responds to arrow keys and q.
Claude Desktop's Code tab no longer blames the connection for certificate signature problems, and Web Search shows its progress while retrying.
Desktop notifications work inside tmux with passthrough and in iTerm2 over SSH, and /copy and /export over SSH no longer claim a copy that may not have happened.
Notice fixes: /usage-credits reports refused requests correctly, the share question closes, old upgrade hints disappear after a reset, and the effort notice no longer repeats while others go missing.
/tui default says what keeps fullscreen on when it can't switch, and a new account's first session uses the same renderer as later ones.
Reduce motion and Show tips in /config now apply everywhere, not just the current folder.

Terminal fixes: tmux 3.7 no longer redraws the whole pane while typing, Option+T toggles thinking over SSH from iTerm2, and /terminal-setup names the tmux settings Shift+Enter needs and is honest about older Windows Terminal.
Terminals using the Program Status Protocol (OSC 7501) and the progress bar now show correctly when Claude is working, waiting on you or suspended.
Fullscreen shows that a prompt is waiting while you're scrolled up, tool group headlines name the running call, and counts and timers are accurate.

More fullscreen fixes: multi-line commands don't fill the screen, ! commands show output at once, opened rows show output and timer, the jump-to-bottom pill stays, and the prompt stays visible in short windows.
Custom status lines no longer vanish or go stale after resizes, /cd or /rename, and "esc to interrupt" shows beside them when it applies.
Screen fixes: no mouse codes in the shell after fullscreen, no Ctrl+Z message over the prompt, claude logs doesn't mix with existing output, and no flicker or jumps as replies and tool calls finish.
The resume preview scrolls in fullscreen, Esc leaves the /ide auto-connect question, first-run setup reports what it changed, and /status shows install warnings once.
The footer's PR badge follows branch switches, and push and PR summaries no longer name the wrong branch or claim a merge gh refused.
Wrapped URLs are clickable in more terminals, and the Ctrl+O transcript gives correct hints and shows Claude is still working.
Small and narrow windows no longer cut off searches, pickers, plan approvals, /context, errors and status lines, and wide tables in plans and prompts render cleanly.
Theme fixes make code, diffs, spinners and /usage bars readable across themes and terminals, and the /effort slider takes clicks in fullscreen.
Text layout fixes for joined emoji and Indic vowel signs, GNU screen, JSON and number indents, diff line numbers after "No newline at end of file", and the hidden-text count on long lines.
Notebook edits always show a tool row, model and effort questions show key hints, the ? list fits small windows, and screen reader mode no longer leaves stray hints after /permissions search.
Bash and Code Mode permission checks are stricter: some commands, including sandboxed ones and ones with very long values, now ask first or are refused where nobody can answer.
When Code Mode can't be turned on, the message now says what you can do.

The Bash sandbox is tightened on macOS, Linux and WSL: mods folder edits ask more often, sandboxed commands write to fewer folders, and Claude learns on Linux that a server is reachable only from the command that started it.
Secrets are masked better in Remote Control and cloud push notifications, and logout retries revoking the login or says where to revoke it.
Remote Control now streams replies from claude remote-control, Claude Desktop and VS Code sessions to your phone or browser as they're written.

Speed and CPU improvements: smoother typing, streaming and resizing, faster responses after file edits (most on Windows), fewer idle wake-ups, lighter tracking of 20+ subagents, and a faster first Bash command on Windows.
Faster first replies after /compact in git repos, for queued Desktop messages, and in new Desktop sessions that no longer wait on on-demand local MCP servers.
PreToolUse updatedInput survives more multi-hook cases, exit code 127 warns the check may not have run, and hook failures, blocks and timeouts are colored with their reason shown.
The folder trust prompt lists the project settings files to be loaded, marks ones that run commands, and says why Claude Code exited.
Non-interactive runs and background agents name the cause when a permission check errors.
Claude in Chrome requests over Remote Control name the target site, and long browser_batch calls get 150 seconds instead of 90.
In cloud sessions, Claude is told the outcome is unknown when an MCP call through the proxy is cut off after sending.
/update-config uses about 13,000 tokens of context instead of 93,000, and rejected edits quote only the changed settings.
Program Status Protocol reports list background commands, monitors and MCP tasks, and an expired Monitor tells Claude about its stderr output and where it is.
/doctor reports findings as it goes, broken JSON in settings or .mcp.json gives line and column, and commands turned off for your setup explain why instead of "Unknown command".
Clearer errors for CERT_SIGNATURE_FAILURE after a CA renewal, an exhausted team budget (with reset time), and a refused Console sign-in (run /login).

Sign-in screens are clearer: wrong pastes are explained, /login uses a real text field, /design-login, /install-github-app and MCP sign-in match it and mask codes, and gateway sign-in links can be copied with c.
/plugin's Discover, Marketplaces, Installed, Errors and Stats tabs fit small windows, support paging keys and clicks, and have clearer confirmations and errors.
Terminal output and wording are made consistent across claude plugin, mcp, update, doctor, sign-in, setup and other commands; JSON and piped output keep their format.
Dialogs get consistent key hints, text fields, ✘ ⚠ ✔ markers and spacing, and deeper /hooks and /permissions screens say Esc goes back.
Lists show how many rows are hidden, wrap at both ends, take Home, End and paging (including agent view pickers), and mark the selected row the same way everywhere.
Small UI changes: a "↓ to resume subagent" hint after Ctrl+C, hidden-line counts on long prompts, new sliders for /autocompact and /scroll-speed, on/off labels, and a clearer "Queued" hint.
Terminal setup lists every change before making it.

Auto mode becomes the default start for HIPAA-configured Cowork organizations and when policy hasn't loaded, server-managed defaultMode wins once settings load, and HIPAA organizations get the server-side classifier.
A managed-mcp.json added mid-session may apply at the next check; restart sessions for it to apply fully.
Code Mode's $ shell helper refuses some values, auto mode stops some commands it used to allow, and some macOS Bash commands now ask or are refused.
A hook's "decision": "block" now holds in more cases, so a hook that always prints it may start blocking calls.

Sandbox changes: its state may persist until /sandbox or /cd, sensitive home folders are no longer writable by default (sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite can allow some), odd .git entries are set aside, and missing --add-dir folders are created on Linux and WSL.

Rewritten commands stay sandboxed unless the approver adds dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true, claude mcp serve ignores sandbox.excludedCommands, and some environment-setting lines ask when auto-allow is off.
With the sandbox on, /rewind leaves some files untouched and reports them as skipped.
File tools refuse writes to Claude Code's sign-in files and some device and process files, and Bash asks before more commands touching sign-in files and before some cp and mv commands.
Some tool calls in bypass permissions mode now ask, or are denied where nobody can be asked.
Worktree-isolated subagents refuse some git commands that could rewrite branches shared with your checkout, and ExitWorktree won't remove a worktree still in use unless Claude passes discard_changes.
The computer use macOS permissions panel ignores j and k; use the arrows or Ctrl+P and Ctrl+N.
The PowerShell tool asks about more commands, even in bypass mode, denies malformed ones, and refuses functions named like built-in commands so Claude can rename them.

Auto mode ignores some loose wildcard allow rules, judges rules whose program is a Windows backslash path, and a managed autoMode.environment without "$defaults" replaces the built-ins in Desktop and SDK apps too.
--add-dir and /add-dir show the trust prompt for untrusted folders in local terminal sessions; claude --bg refuses them.
Self-hosted runners with --trust-workspace false ignore more repository settings, and "always allow" answers over Remote Control and on runners are saved differently.
Enabled plugins previously refused for a malformed plugin.json display field now load with their hooks and MCP servers; administrators should review the plugins they deploy.
allowedHttpHookUrls and httpHookAllowedEnvVars apply differently to managed hooks, and HTTP hooks ignore Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in their headers.
Uninstalling a plugin deletes its extracted MCP bundle files unless shared, some worktree sessions skip plugin settings with a notice, and /plugin questions use lists instead of y, n and u.
Automatic compaction in plan mode uses the model answering you, such as Opus with opusplan, which can cost more.
Cowork cloud sessions hold OpenTelemetry export until the first turn, so claude_code.session.count can drop.

Cross-machine messages are refused when an API key or similar sits beside a claude.ai login, --bare background sessions on unapproved keys are refused, and auto-continue at a usage limit stops if your login changes.
Remote Control connects through proxies with a CONNECT tunnel (proxies that refuse it now stop it), and its --verbose debug logs go to ~/.claude/child-logs/.
Self-hosted runner sessions without gh get a built-in gh api via Anthropic by default; --use-anthropic-gh false turns it off.
Quitting agent view from an empty conversation ends that session, --await-initialize is refused with --bg or --worktree --tmux, and worktree, /teleport and IDE checkouts run git with a stricter PATH.
Approving a subagent's plan now offers two choices: Yes and switch to default mode for the session, or No.
The /claude-api skill builds agents on Managed Agents by default unless you want to host the loop yourself.
/usage in fullscreen shows plan limit bars before cost for subscribers, first-run setup preselects the Auto theme, and fullscreen /cd won't accept Yes while its trust prompt doesn't fit.
The tmux mouse wheel notice and the spinner tip suggesting /clear after 30 minutes are removed.
VS Code adds claudeCode.promptSuggestions to turn prompt suggestions off.
In VS Code, "Rewind code to here" in a forked conversation no longer undoes an extra turn, and the Sandbox dialog no longer creates empty files while the sandbox is off.
VS Code sign-in fixes: saved sign-in survives some networks, wrong pastes are explained, the sign-in screen no longer flashes for Console users, and "Request more" works after signing in again.
/ide from a second session no longer silently steals the editor connection; the newest wins and the other shows how to switch back.
The VS Code Memory dialog handles symlink loops and named pipes, and live command output keeps flowing after a failed read.
VS Code explains why "Open in Terminal" couldn't start claude, shows "Open artifact" links, keeps the attach hint visible, and fixes high-contrast theme visuals.
VS Code skips waiting for problems on unopened files during Edit and Write, styles live output like the command card, and keeps extension errors out of the editor's telemetry.
